deterministic_rule_draft.prompt:
Create a sunlit, compact fragment of a Hong Kong neighborhood against an open blue sky. Suspend this irregular L- or cross-shaped urban island over an empty pale-blue void, with no surrounding terrain. End its sidewalks, roads, and buildings abruptly at sheer vertical cut edges that expose plain building backs; make the perimeter uneven and stark, composed of simple wall masses.

Arrange roughly twenty densely packed, mid-rise residential and mixed-use buildings organically beside two narrow streets meeting at a small offset intersection. Detail the inner streets with yellow curb lines, yellow zebra crossings, white lane markings, small traffic islands, railings, bollards, signs, lamps, hydrants, bins, utility boxes, manholes, and a fenced orange roadwork area containing barriers and cones. Keep the urban core richly detailed and convincingly dense.

Most buildings should be six- to ten-story concrete apartment blocks: flat-roofed, with muted pink, cream, gray, brown, and green stucco or tile façades, narrow gaps, varied setbacks, and occasional rounded street corners. Turn detailed façades toward the roads and leave tall, largely blank walls facing outward. Along the ground floors, form a continuous cluttered band of shuttered storefronts, recessed doors, awnings, Chinese and English signs, graffiti, lanterns, and hanging pennant flags. Equip upper façades with gridded metal-framed windows, enclosed balconies, projecting air-conditioning units, drainpipes, cables, laundry racks, and colorful clothes. Pack the flat roofs with corrugated extensions, water or utility housings, railings, antenna frames, satellite dishes, ducts, and small mechanical boxes.
